legacy.note: Input: the legacy test recorded each snapshot by patching operation_trace.atomic_replace with a recording replace; the new test records every atomic_replace the sink starts, with the snapshot bytes that call received, through sys.monitoring (ObservedCalls), and joins the sink's pending timer instead of polling with time.sleep.

Input: the legacy test polled progress with time.sleep until the lagging snapshot showed only the parent; the new test joins the sink's pending timer (the thread that writes that snapshot) and then makes the same assertion on the snapshot.

Input: the legacy test made the patched atomic_replace raise PermissionError(13, 'private request value'); the new test makes the real replace fail (a directory holds the snapshot's name) and checks that the message and strerror of that same OS error, reproduced by calling file_io.atomic_replace on the same target, are not in the record, which it also compares field by field.

Input: the legacy test passed the real LocalHost to activation_requirements; the new test passes the counting fake host (ObservedHost) and asserts it was asked for no observation, so the host cannot change the judged requirements.

Input: the legacy test wrote a high-water a minute after its fixed engine clock into the runtime; the new test keeps the published high-water and moves the clock port's wall clock a minute before it, the same relation.

Input: the legacy test ran _activate_initialization and then FakeEngine.activate (synthetic evidence applied to an in-memory engine, adapter_for patched) on one engine; the new test runs _activate_initialization on a publicly initialized instance and checks the public activation of the same initialization (the restored Sim.activated template, which the process built from an initialized Sim through controls and owner passes).
Input: the legacy test wrote a high-water a day after its fixed engine clock into the runtime; the new test moves the clock port's wall clock a day before the published high-water, the same relation.

Input: the legacy test replaced the engine's two clock functions with datetime.now and time.monotonic and spaced samples with time.sleep(.002); the new test gives the engine the product's real clock port (SystemClock) and spaces the samples by two milliseconds of the monotonic clock.

Input: the legacy test patched do_math.lifecycle_engine.time.get_clock_info, which is the attribute of the standard time module; the new test patches time.get_clock_info, the same object, without naming a product module, and moves the clock port's monotonic and wall clocks instead of replacing the engine's clock functions.

Input: the legacy test built an engine without __init__ holding only the policy continue_authorized and no conversations; the new test uses the public activation, which adopted continue_authorized, and asserts that policy and that no conversation exists before the same judgment.

Input: the legacy test ran the child process against a repository git_init made; the new test runs the same child process against a Sim's repository, which the command never opens because it refuses the decision's shape first, and checks the Sim's inbox.

Input: the legacy test replaced cli.ResearchEngine with a Mock whose run returned {'status': 'waiting'} and checked its call arguments; the new test runs cli.execute on a CLI-created instance, records the engine run's arguments and the object it returned through sys.monitoring, and asserts the command returns that same object. The watching run of an idle initializing instance never ends by itself, so a pause is sent when the owner first waits on the clock port between passes, and the returned status is therefore 'paused'. No model call starts (ModelRunner.run is never entered).

Input: the legacy test patched windows_job.named_job_empty and owner_ended to return True; the new test gives the launch ticket an owner whose process ID now names another process (another creation time) on the Jobs port, whose owner_ended and named_job_empty the test asserts report True before the recovery runs. Start state: the legacy class ran on active_instance restored with CURRENTNESS_CONFIG (max_input_bytes 2,000,000, tool_review_window_seconds 60, self_check_response_window_seconds 5, scholarly and operator off); the restored public activation holds the same values (the product default 2,000,000, the two windows the activation configures, and the Sim's scholarly and operator off).

Input: the legacy test called the method on an engine built without __init__ that held only the question; the new test calls it on the restored public activation's engine whose question links are that one question.

Input: the legacy test sent configure, request, status and close through the CLI on the synthetic active state, wrote the new profiles' capability evidence by hand and ran ScriptedRunner in real Windows Jobs; the new test sends the same public controls the CLI sends (each applied by the owner as the command does) on the restored public activation, reads the status the CLI's status --json returns (engine.status), records capability evidence with the public probe decision over the fake host, and runs the maintenance call through the worker and the model double. The command surface itself (request --retry-action reaching the inbox idempotently) is boundary.test_engine_cli.CliTests.test_retry_action_reaches_the_public_control_inbox_idempotently. The closed-instance refusal is a ValueError of the public control with the exact message, where the CLI reported it as exit code 2 with that message.

Input and a changed expected value: the legacy test replaced engine._provider_admit with a stub that wrote dispatch_wait {'kind': 'capacity', 'provider': 'test-double'} and refused. The new test lets the product's admission refuse: the Codex gate is closed by a reported usage limit (SessionSlots.provider_result_from_run) at the start of _provider_admit, seen through a sys.monitoring start event, after the dispatch check passed and the input was prepared; the gate reopens when the clock passes its retry time. The deferred execution's disposition kind is therefore the product's provider_limit where the stub wrote capacity: maintenance profiles hold no capacity reference, so a capacity refusal cannot occur for this action.

Input: the legacy fixture held the action on context_engine (an engine without __init__ with autospec store, session slots and clock over record_fixtures.approved_task); the new fixture holds the same action, activity wait and profiles on the restored public activation's engine through the product's task, activity and profile functions (support.engine_overflow.held_work).

Input: held on the Sim as for test_overflow_choices_are_supplied_without_changing_ready_population. The wiring from a planner's submitted extension to _apply_input_overflow_resolutions, which this test enters directly, runs in flows.test_engine_input_recovery.OverflowGitConnection.test_plan_choice_repackages_original_work_and_reaches_runner.

Input: the legacy test replaced the engine's runner with a local runner in real Windows Jobs that wrote the planner's extension and failed on any other role; the new test runs both calls through the worker and the model double, writes the same extension inside the planner's call (ScenarioModel.during) and asserts the exact list of roles called after each owner pass. The two profiles' capability evidence is the product's capability_evidence over the fake host's observation of each profile, where the legacy test used FixtureAdapter's description.

Input: the legacy walkthrough built evidence_engine (an engine without __init__, a synthetic approved charter and an input-snapshot store double); the new one uses the restored public activation, whose charter the user's public decision replaces with one carrying the academic requirement. The accepted knowledge is recorded in memory as in the legacy engine_fixtures.accept_knowledge (a synthetic verified result and identity match under the instance's active trust environment).

Input: the legacy walkthrough replaced engine._issued_input with an autospec returning no available inputs and put the running execution into the runtime as a bare record; the new one archives that issued input below the preparation's input bundle (the engine reads it back), registers the running execution with the engine's _register_execution, and offers the adopted research_work profile editions (the Sim also holds editions a later configuration replaced, which the profile selection refuses to choose among).

Changed expected value and input: the legacy evidence_engine set goal_status to 'unresolved', a value outside the product's goal status vocabulary (initialize_state and governance use 'unsolved' and 'mathematically_solved'), and the walkthrough asserted that the not_satisfied audit left it; the new instance starts at the product's 'unsolved' and the walkthrough asserts it stays exactly 'unsolved'. The plan reads the snapshot published before the knowledge was accepted in memory, because the storage contract refuses to publish the synthetic identity match (a match needs a sealed review cycle); the legacy store double served the same tasks and ready task IDs. The legacy sentinel value also failed the walkthrough if the unsatisfied audit wrote any goal status; the new walkthrough keeps that discrimination by asserting that goal_assessment_basis is the same before and after the audit.

Input: each charter goal is adopted by the user's public decision on the restored public activation instead of a new evidence_engine; the walkthrough asserts that no goal judgment existed before the audit, so goal_judgments[0] is this audit's.
Input: the context's goal is the current charter's (governance_view), where the legacy evidence_engine carried it as the governance_working_view projection on the instance.

Input: the legacy walkthrough loaded review_fixtures.reviewed_candidate into evidence_engine and published only the knowledge families to a new git_init repository; the new one starts from theorem k1 that the Lean double verified and a sealed identity review matched on the restored public activation, publishes the engine's whole state, writes the Sim's Git objects out as loose objects, and queries through query_records and read_record on the real Git process (they take no Ports).

Input: the legacy vector wrote capability evidence from the real local adapter's identity for evidence_engine's profiles and put the running execution into the runtime as a bare record; the new one uses the capability evidence the public activation's probe recorded over the fake host, registers the running execution with _register_execution in its opened activity, and ends it through the product's lifecycle transitions.
